text:
miriam: short write-up from today's sync: propose a lightweight 'fitness' gate for model ingest. goal: catch obvious incompat/latency/tokenizer issues quickly and avoid running full bench on obviously broken artifacts.

ken: nice. can you list the concrete checks we run in the fast-path?

miriam: minimal checks: (A) artifact manifest & signature (shapes, ops) (B) tokenizer roundtrip checks on 50 short/gold prompts (C) microprofile: 3 seq-lens at batch 1 and batch 8 (D) compact perf fingerprint vector + shape_hash (E) deterministic golden-output smoke (fast) + policy hint.

olivia: microprofile storage question 12: how long do we keep traces?

miriam: keep aggregates (p50/p95/p99, mem) in primary store for 90 days. full traces go to cold storage only on CAUTIOUS/HOLD results.

samir: curious about fingerprint compare; what's the comparator and thresholds? also how big is the vector?

miriam: plan: cosine similarity + a few rule checks (max latency delta > 30% => flag; tokenizer vocab cover drop > 0.5% => flag). vector = ~64 dims, final serialized < 1KB. comparator returns a small enum: OK / WARN / DIVERGENT + delta metrics.

ingest-bot: ingest pipeline queued: https://ci.redwood/ingest/4823456789/results (will attach raw microprofile once job completes)

ken: edge case: two variants (fp16 vs int8) often have similar outputs but different perf fingerprints. we should compare fingerprints only within the same compile/qprofile.

miriam: agreed. namespace fingerprint by (model_name, commit_hash, compile_profile, qprofile).

olivia: UI/registry changes: we need a status history per artifact: PASS / CAUTIOUS / HOLD + human message + link to traces. I'll draft a migration plan to add fields: fingerprint_vector, fingerprint_version, gate_status_history.

samir: rollout behavior question: if fast gate returns WARN (fingerprint drift) but deterministic outputs match, do we block or canary?

miriam: canonical behavior: WARN -> CAUTIOUS -> auto-canary 5-10% for 24h with continuous eval suite. HOLD -> block ingest and notify safety/ops. Teams can override with justification, but override triggers post-ingest deep-evals.

ken: do we need a checksum for the tokenizer vocab file? some uploaders accidentally truncate.

miriam: yes - tokenizer file sha256 included in manifest check; tokenizer roundtrip also detects truncated mapping by high OOV rates.

olivia: sample fingerprint snippet for the registry (for the schema PR):
```json
{
  "fp_version": "1",
  "dims": 64,
  "hotpath": {"p50_ms": "12.3", "p95_ms": "45.2"},
  "tokenizer": {"vocab_coverage": "0.997", "sha256": "sha256:deadbeef"},
  "shape_hash": "sha256:faceb00c",
  "vector_base64": "AAECAwQ..."
}
```

samir: good. I'll draft the canary/rollback playbook: include automatic rollback on quality delta > X and manual escalation path.

miriam: action items: @ken - build comparator stub (cosine + rule thresholds) by Tue; @olivia - registry migration + UI fields + retention proposal; @samir - canary playbook draft; I'll update ingest job to call gatelet and emit telemetry events.

ken: SGTM, will spin up a tiny test pool with one GPU for the microprofile runs.

olivia: will open the migration PR later today.

samir: will sketch the playbook and sample eval sets.

miriam: if we're happy with this scope I'll collect notes into a short RFC draft after prototypes. react :thumbsup: to push forward or :eyes: if you want to discuss more.

ken: :thumbsup:

olivia: :eyes:

samir: :thumbsup:

ingest-bot: ticket updated -> RED-INGEST-512: https://go.redwood/RED-INGEST-512

miriam: thanks all. filing RFC once the comparator prototype lands.
